open_questions: Gaia/centroid_all not run leaves on-target location formally unconfirmed; high-resolution follow-up (RV or difference imaging) can confirm the dip is on TIC 0.3029 R_sun M dwarf

duration ratio 1.763 (observed 1.493 h vs central 0.8466 h) with fit_log_density_ratio -2.297 and star_density_penalty 140.5 indicates transit is longer and shallower than central for this star — likely due to modest eccentricity and spot dilution rather than stellar binarity, but needs RV to rule out NEB fully
dossier.public_summary: A consistent ~6000 ppm flat-bottom dip repeats every 1.02 days for 37 transits on a small spotted M dwarf and matches a ~2.6 Earth-radius planet, with no secondary eclipse or odd-even difference and no nearby star able to mimic the depth. The rotation period happens to be the same by chance, and the transit is longer than central, which is expected for a short-period small-planet orbit around an active star and not a sign of a stellar companion.

reasons.why: strongly flat-bottomed (negative v_sigma) positively favours a transit over a V-shaped eclipsing binary; fit_b 0.1709 low-impact though fit_k near grazing is later explained by density mismatch
planet-sized with undiluted_depth_ppm 6371 and rp_over_rstar 0.07982, far below stellar regime
no secondary detected (snr 0.7232, depth_over_dip 0.06437, best_brightening_snr 6.817) and odd_even.diff_sigma 1.008 shows no odd/even difference, disfavouring binary at twice period

centroid is inconclusive (no sector with a clear difference image, SNR_diff 1.343 and -1.664 used=false) but nearest star that could cause the dip is 43.1 arcsec (29 TESS pixels) needing 0.2873 eclipse, and could_cause_within_1px is 0, so no neighbour can plausibly produce the 6370 ppm dip
37 transits are consistent for a low SNR 11.14 signal around a 27283 ppm spotted M dwarf; share_of_top_3 0.336 and no outliers, so variability does not explain signal as a few bad events or spots

depth change 58.22% between sector 46 TESS-SPOC 6458+/-746 ppm and sector 91 QLP 3546+/-1194 ppm is explained by one product per sector and different uncertainties; p_constant_all 0.038607632313089606 is above 0.01 and verdict is steady

scorer rates as low planet-like, but specific positive evidence above — flat bottom, no secondary, no odd/even, no plausible neighbour, and consistent depth across 37 events — that scorer cannot fully credit for an active M dwarf overrides the low rank; similar neighbours include 4 planet outcomes vs 1 not a planet

period coincidence (signal 1.01578 d vs rotation 1.018 d) is present but rotation tool amplitudes are 27283 ppm and 28324 ppm vs depth 6077 ppm with shape v_sigma -1.452 flat and no phase_curve swing large enough to match depth, so period equality by chance around a spotted star does not favour variability over a planet
